name: Budj Bim National Park
bio_draft: Volcanic landscape and World Heritage Gunditjmara eel-trap aquaculture system.

facts.claim: National park in Victoria's Western District about 270 km west of Melbourne, co-managed with Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners
Visitor area has a crater lake, lava canals and lava caves, with four walking options
Park forms part of the Gunditjmara cultural landscape, an Aboriginal cultural landscape
Tae Rak Aquaculture Centre, 30 min away, runs guided cultural tours and has a kooyang (eel) display tank

name: Lake Surprise
bio_draft: Crater lake that is the main attraction of Budj Bim National Park, with walking trails and a lava cave nearby.

facts.claim: Crater lake in Budj Bim National Park, walkable from the campground
Lake Surprise Walk descends from the lookout to the lake's edge
Longer Lava Canal Circuit Walk passes lava blisters, Tunnel Cave, Natural Bridge and a dry crater with views over the lake

Emus, kangaroos, koalas, swans and ducks live inside the crater

facts.claim: Brackish volcanic crater lake near Camperdown, paired with neighbouring Lake Gnotuk
Maximum depth about 66 m

name: Lake Gnotuk
bio_draft: Smaller volcanic crater lake beside Lake Bullen Merri, with a rim walk.

facts.claim: Lake Gnotuk is the smaller northern neighbour of Lake Bullen Merri, a pair of crater lakes near Camperdown in south-western Victoria.
Gnotuk is hypersaline, about twice as salty as seawater, with a maximum depth of about 20 m.
The crater is about 2 km across, with shore terraces marking past higher water levels.

name: Colac
bio_draft: Main town of the Otways region, on the shore of Lake Colac, a base for the Otways and the volcanic lakes.

facts.claim: Colac is a town in the Western District of Victoria, about 150 km south-west of Melbourne.
It sits on the southern shore of Lake Colac.

name: Kara Kara National Park
bio_draft: Forest and hills north of Ararat, listed as a regional bushwalking and nature stop.

facts.claim: Kara Kara National Park is a 13,990-hectare park in the Wimmera/Goldfields region, about 190 km north-west of Melbourne, south of St Arnaud.
It protects one of the largest intact areas of Box-Ironbark forest in Victoria, with 275 recorded native flora species.
The flat Upper Teddington Reservoir Walk is 2.8 km, with good bird watching; the park also has rocky ridge lookouts and camping at Teddington.
It is jointly managed by the Dja Dja Wurrung Clans Aboriginal Corporation and Parks Victoria.

access_note: Parks Victoria page lists no entry fee (Victorian national parks are free); page template contains a generic 'area is closed' banner label, not verified as an actual closure

name: Brim Silo Art
bio_draft: Silo mural at Brim on the Silo Art Trail, a short roadside stop.

facts.claim: Guido van Helten's mural was the first silo artwork in Victoria and inspired the Silo Art Trail.
It is part of the Silo Art Trail, a 700 km outdoor gallery of silo murals through the Wimmera Mallee.
The mural spans four 1939-built GrainCorp silos and depicts a quartet of farmers.
